title: The British Pound sets a new September low as Fed officials argue for more
body: 1.3400 has capped GBP/USD in every session since the Fed raised rates on September 16. The pair went through that level on the day of the decision and has failed to get back above it four times since.

title: US Crude Inventories Rise 1.79M Barrels
body: US crude oil inventories increased by 1.786 million barrels in the week ending September 18, following a sharp build of 7.14 million barrels in the prior week. Over the past 23 weeks, commercial crude stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) have fallen by a cumulative 39 million barrels, yet they remain nearly 12 million barrels higher year-to-date. During the week ending September 18, an additional 400,000 barrels were released from the SPR to support commercial inventories, reducing SPR holdings to 284.6 million barrels. This level remains within the commonly cited operational range of 250 million to 300 million barrels. At Cushing, Oklahoma, the key delivery hub, inventories rose by 2.082 million barrels after a 246,000-barrel draw the previous week. US crude oil production was unchanged at 13.944 million barrels per day in the week ending September 11, an increase of 462,000 barrels per day compared with the same period a year earlier. On the product side, gasoline inventories fell by 2.16 million barrels, while distillate stocks decreased by 2.164 million barrels. title: Ibovespa Rises on US-Iran Talks Hopes
body: The Ibovespa advanced 0.4% to close at 187,423, rebounding from earlier losses on optimism over potential talks between the United States and Iran. US President Donald Trump said American officials held a "very good" meeting with Iranian representatives on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and that another round of talks was planned. A senior Iranian official indicated that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days if Washington eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports. The partial unwinding of the recent oil rally underpinned equity markets. Among financials, performance was mixed: Banco do Brasil and Santander retreated 1.4% and 0.6%, respectively, while Bradesco and Itaú advanced 1.5% and 0.2%. Petrobras gained 0.7% despite softer oil prices. Vale added 0.4% after confirming the acquisition of a 30% stake in Ligga, and Axia climbed 1.3%. The Ibovespa remained volatile throughout the session, as investors reacted to the Central Bank's Copom minutes, which were interpreted as somewhat hawkish. title: South Korea's Consumer Confidence Rises to 106.6 in September, Signaling Stronger Sentiment
body: South Korea's consumer confidence strengthened in September 2026, with the headline index climbing to 106.6 from 104.5 in August 2026. The latest data, updated on 22 September 2026, indicates an improvement in household sentiment and suggests growing optimism about economic conditions. The move further into positive territory — above the neutral 100 mark — points to increasing willingness among consumers to spend, which could support domestic demand in the coming months. While detailed drivers of the rise were not disclosed, the steady month-on-month gain underscores a gradual recovery in confidence heading into the latter part of 2026. title: TSX Hits Over Two-Week High
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index rose 0.9% to close at 36,336, its highest level in more than two weeks, as investors weighed the outlook for prospective US–Iran talks. US President Trump said American officials had a "very good" meeting with Iranian envoys on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and indicated that another round of discussions was being planned in the near future. A senior Iranian official signaled that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports. A pause in the recent oil rally—which has stoked inflationary pressures and driven central banks to raise interest rates—provided support for equities. Miners advanced alongside a rebound in gold prices, with Agnico Eagle up 3.4%, Barrick gaining 3.1%, and WPM adding 4.5%. Shopify jumped 7.4% after announcing a partnership with Meta that will allow purchases through Meta's Muse AI agent using Shop Pay. In contrast, financials finished lower after Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem cautioned that future rate decisions will have to weigh sluggish economic growth against elevated energy costs. title: U.S. API Crude Inventories Drop Sharply, Hinting at Tighter Oil Market
body: U.S. crude oil inventories tracked by the American Petroleum Institute (API) rose by 1.786 million barrels in the latest week, a significantly smaller build than the prior reading of 7.140 million barrels. The data, updated on 22 September 2026, point to a marked slowdown in stock accumulation, suggesting a potential tightening in supply-demand balances. The pullback from the previous, much larger inventory increase may indicate firmer demand, lower imports, shifts in refinery runs, or a combination of these factors. While crude stocks are still rising, the deceleration is likely to draw attention from traders and analysts assessing the outlook for U.S. supply and its implications for global oil prices. Market participants will now look to confirm these signals against official U.S. government inventory data and upcoming refinery and demand figures. Any sustained trend toward smaller builds—or a move into outright draws—could reinforce expectations of a tighter market heading into the next quarter. title: Oil Extends Losses on US-Iran Diplomacy Hopes
body: Crude oil fell below $90 a barrel on Tuesday, extending losses for a fifth consecutive session after US President Donald Trump disclosed that Washington had held three hours of talks with Iran on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. In his address to the UN, Trump said he faced a "big decision" over whether to pursue a negotiated agreement with Iran or "annihilate the Islamic Republic," adding that he believed a deal would likely come after the election. A senior Iranian government official said Tehran's proposal has been relayed to Washington. The plan calls for the resumption of negotiations aimed at permanently ending hostilities. If the US moves to lift the blockade that has sharply curtailed Iranian oil exports, Iran would be ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, the official said. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia is reportedly preparing to restart its key East–West pipeline, targeting the restoration of significant volumes by Saturday. title: US Stocks Close Mixed Amid Yields Rebound
body: US equity markets ended mixed on Tuesday as a rebound in Treasury yields capped gains in chipmakers. The S&P 500 finished little changed, while the Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.8% to a record close of 30,732 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 185 points. Another strong session for AI-related names supported the broader market. AI infrastructure stocks outperformed, helped by a robust reception to Meta's new Muse AI agent. In parallel, Anthropic announced a new AI model aimed at handling a broad range of business tasks at lower cost, ahead of its highly anticipated Wall Street debut. Large semiconductor names underpinned the Nasdaq's advance. Nvidia gained 0.7%, Micron added 5%, and Sandisk surged 6.8% after an upgrade from Rosenblatt. The S&P 500 trimmed earlier losses after President Trump said US officials had a "very good" meeting with Iranian representatives. Manufacturer shares also firmed, with Applied Materials rising 1.8%. By contrast, weakness in financials weighed on the Dow. Bank stocks came under pressure, with JPMorgan sliding 3.4% and Bank of America down 3% amid the sector-wide selloff.
